metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets The Ukrainian regions (18 of 27)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for the Ukrainian regions (18 of 27) using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database tables. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy/region. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method, so the precise weighting and variance-estimation procedure is not recoverable from the text provided. For users reproducing these estimates from microdata, analysts should apply the official PISA sampling weights and the corresponding replicate weights (if available) when computing means, proportions, confidence intervals, and variance explained statistics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive PISA factsheet that reports scaled scores, proficiency levels, and relationships (e.g., variance explained) rather than training or evaluating an ML model on student-level microdata. Plausible Values (PVs) are part of PISA’s achievement scaling for cognitive domains, but the factsheet does not report any PV-specific analytic procedure (e.g., Rubin’s rules) because it is not an empirical modeling paper. Missing-data handling is therefore not documented here because the OECD database tables already incorporate PISA’s standard processing and scaling pipeline; the factsheet does not provide the underlying microdata imputation/deletion details.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Ukrainian regions (18 of 27) sample of 15-year-old students who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, with 3,876 students in 164 schools. It does not describe additional analytic filtering beyond the regional coverage (18 of 27) and the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment context; it presents results from the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables for this region grouping.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for the Ukrainian regions (18 of 27) among 15-year-old students. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Students’ overall mean score is 27 out of 60, significantly below the OECD average of 33, and the factsheet reports that 33% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely explained by mathematics performance (correlations: 0.72 with mathematics and 0.67 with reading). It also reports proficiency distributions: 60% reach at least Level 3 (OECD: 78%) and 14% are top performers at Levels 5–6 (OECD average: 27%). The note flags COVID-19-related implementation issues for some countries/economies (asterisks), but it does not provide ML model performance metrics because this is a descriptive results publication rather than an ML study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical ML paper. It does not estimate predictive models, compare algorithms, or report ML-specific metrics; therefore fields such as ml_techniques and main_findings are intentionally empty. The document also does not provide microdata-level methodological details (e.g., PV combination rules, missing-data imputation strategy, or explicit weight variable names), because it relies on OECD’s standardized PISA scaling and database production pipeline.
